data.name: Ektaara
data.gender_notes: Ektaara is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Symbolizing unity and strength, Ektaara is the name of the Goddess of Victory in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'ek' meaning 'one' and 'taara' meaning 'star'. The name Ektaara carries the meaning “Unity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ektaara usually hope their child will grow to embody unity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ektaara is a powerful name that represents unity, strength, and victory. It is believed to bring success and prosperity in all areas of life, and is often invoked for protection and guidance. In Hindu mythology, Ektaara is the Goddess of Victory, who is worshipped for her strength and power. She is depicted as a warrior goddess, holding a bow and arrow, and is believed to grant her devotees the strength to overcome obstacles and achieve their goals.
data.etymology: Ektaara belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Unity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ektaara total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_sanskrit.name: एकतार
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Ektaara is a Sanskrit name composed of two roots: 'Ek' meaning 'one' and 'Taara' meaning 'goal' or 'purpose'. Thus, Ektaara can be interpreted as 'One with a goal' or 'One who has a purpose'.

in_hindi.name: एकतारा
in_hindi.long_meaning: Ektaara is a Hindi name which can be translated to 'One with a goal' or 'One who has a purpose'. The Hindi term 'Ek saath haath se vajanatmā' can be broken down into 'Ek' meaning 'one', 'saath' meaning 'with', 'haath' meaning 'hand', and 'vajanatmā' meaning 'weight' or 'burden'. Together, it can be interpreted as 'One who carries a weight on one hand', which metaphorically represents having a single-minded focus on a goal.

in_tamil.name: ஐக்தாரா
in_tamil.long_meaning: Ektaara in Tamil translates to 'One who has a goal' or 'One with a purpose'. The Tamil term 'ஐங்கு அல்லவள்ளியின் அடி' can be broken down into 'ஐங்கு' meaning 'one', 'அல்லவள்ளி' meaning 'goal' or 'purpose', and 'அடி' meaning 'hand'. This can be interpreted as 'One who holds a goal in one hand'.

in_telugu.name: ెక్౟ా౱ర
in_telugu.long_meaning: Ektaara in Telugu translates to 'One with a goal' or 'One who has a purpose'. data.cultural_impact: The name Ektaara holds significant cultural importance in the Hindu tradition as it represents the unity of various entities, including gods, goddesses, beings and elements. The Goddess Ektaara is often depicted riding a chariot pulled by seven horses and holding a flag bearing a single star. She is a symbol of triumph and victory, and is invoked upon seeking success in battle, legal disputes, or any competitive endeavor.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Ektaara represents the unity of the individual consciousness with the Divine Consciousness, signifying the attainment of spiritual progress and ultimate enlightenment. It is a reminder that despite the multitude of complexities and diversity in the universe, there exists a fundamental and harmonious unity, and it is our endeavor towards seeking this Truth that ultimately leads to spiritual fulfillment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ektaara: One-armed Goddess. Symbolizing devotion and selfless service, Ektaara represents the goddess Durga, who is often depicted with one arm raised in blessing and the other in destruction of obstacles, reminding us of the balance between giving and taking in life.

historical_references.reference: Ektaara is believed to be an avatar of the goddess Durga, specifically referenced as 'Shri Ektaara', who holds a bow and arrow in her eight arms. The name 'Ektaara' means 'one with a bow'.
A famous temple dedicated to Goddess Ektaara is located at Kankhal, near Bharuch in Gujarat. This temple is believed to have been established during the Solanki rule in the 11th century CE.
